question_text: Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators?

official_answers.text: To more closely follow public opinion

why_it_matters.text: House members with 2-year terms feel public opinion fast. They vote on what people care about right now. The Senate, with 6-year terms, can take a longer view — including making unpopular calls when needed. The two chambers were designed to balance each other.

fun_fact.text: There's a famous old story: When Jefferson returned from France in 1789, he asked Washington why the Convention created a Senate. Washington pointed to Jefferson's saucer of cooling tea: 'We pour legislation into the senatorial saucer to cool it.'

mnemonic.link_sentence: House = hot tea (passionate, fast, 2-year terms); Senate = saucer that cools it (deliberative, slow, 6-year terms).
